newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end sharply lower on Brazil fears.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end sharply lower on Brazil fears.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed sharply lower Tuesday on steady selling blamed on currency fears in Brazil, dealers said.
"The market continued falling today because of the nosedive on the Brazilian markets, but this may be a good opportunity to buy," said Nestor de Cessare at traders Allaria Ledesma.
The blue chip MerVal index tumbled 3.37 percent to 807.91 after closing off 1.7 percent Monday.
The MerVal now stands at a four-week low.

Traders noted while Brazilian officials were denying a sharp devaluation like recent ones in Southeast Asia, Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said on a visit to Washington that any currency movements in Brazil would be small and not affect Argentina.

"Fernandez seemed to be confirming something will happen, which sent jitters through the bolsa. But there was no difficulty trading, because both buyers and sellers were out in force and prices should soon level out," another trader said.
Floor volume swelled to 39.6 million pesos from Monday's weak 20.1 million while over-the-counter turnover picked up to 117.3 million pesos from a token tally of 31.5 million Tuesday.
"Today the pension funds snapped up some positions, especially in stocks traded strictly locally, which will help to underpin the market," De Cessare said.
The broad market closed off 2.4 percent, with losers smashing winners 59 to three and four stocks closing flat.
All main-tier stocks posted losses, led by textile firm and shoemaker Alpargatas, which tumbled 6.9 percent.
Other heavy losers were holding company Comercial del Plata, bank Bansud and Telefonica, off 6.1 percent, 5.7 percent and 3.9 percent, respectively.
